Create the file case_120.inp in the current working directory using the exact input deck content provided.
Run CalculiX by executing the command ccx -i case_120 in the working directory. If that command fails, fall back to ccx case_120.
After the run completes, read the file case_120.sta and determine success by checking for the string JOB COMPLETED (case-insensitive).
Record the CalculiX version string by running ccx -v (or the closest equivalent such as ccx --version) and capture the output.
Write a file named results.json in the working directory containing a JSON object with the following keys: solver set to the string "calculix", case_id set to the string "case_120", status set to "success" if the .sta file indicates job completion or "error" otherwise, ccx_version set to the version string obtained from the version query, artifacts set to a JSON array listing the file names of all output artifacts produced by the run (e.g., .frd, .dat, .sta, .log files), and notes set to a string containing the exact ccx command that was executed; if the run failed, append the error message and the name of the file that indicated the failure.
Do not modify the physics or any values in the input deck.
The reference text containing expected displacements, forces, and stresses at t=10 is provided for verification context only and must not alter the input deck or the commands used.
